questions.q: Recite «لَآ أُقْسِمُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ» (90:1) and name each madd.
questions.a: لَآ: munfasil (4 counts); بِهَٰذَا: natural (2 counts).

questions.q: Sort (pupil PDF): put «جَآءَ», «لَآ أُقْسِمُ», «مَالًا», «وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ», «أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ» into natural, muttasil or munfasil. Today's rota group recites 90:15 to 20.
questions.a: Natural: مَالًا; muttasil: جَآءَ, أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ; munfasil: لَآ أُقْسِمُ, وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ.

questions.q: Extend: explain why we stretch munfasil less, or not at all, when we stop on the first word.
questions.a: When we stop, the hamza is not read, so there is no reason to lengthen it.

questions.q: Stretch: find a munfasil in Al-Fajr 89:16.

questions.a: A) Madd munfasil. The alif ends وَمَآ and the hamza starts أَدْرَىٰكَ: separated, so munfasil.

questions.q: Think again: Munfasil means 'separated'. If muttasil is joined in one word, what is separated in munfasil?
questions.a: The madd letter is at the end of one word and the hamza at the start of the next: separated into two words.
